details.text: A gradual increase in thunderstorm coverage is expected this afternoon along with a corresponding risk for isolated severe weather. A severe thunderstorm watch is not currently expected due to the limited nature of the threat

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Ahead of a vorticity maximum pivoting from the lower Great Lakes into Hudson Valley, visible satellite and radar imagery indicate several areas of deepening moist convection. The 12Z Buffalo and Pittsburgh soundings indicate little to no capping with MLCAPE increasing to 1000-1500 J/kg by afternoon in areas that receive stronger heating. Accordingly, expect a gradual increase in thunderstorm coverage over the next few hours with the 12Z HREF calibrated thunder and paintball plots indicating the highest concentration of storms across the Hudson Valley this afternoon along a persistent zone of low-level confluence. Current VWPs and RAP-based forecast data indicate 30-35 kt of southwesterly deep-layer shear across the region; however, the vector orientation is expected to largely parallel that of the evolving convective bands, limiting the potential for a more organized damaging wind threat. Nonetheless, isolated occurrences of damaging wind gusts appear possible in areas where steeper low-level lapse rates can develop. Additionally, relatively cool mid-level temperatures will be supportive of a marginally severe hail risk with the strongest updrafts
